rationale: "Borrowing limits" is a <div class="h2"> styled to look like a heading. Sighted readers see a heading; the accessibility tree contains no heading at all, so the page has zero headings and cannot be navigated by heading — the primary way screen-reader users move through a long document. The visual hierarchy is real and the programmatic one is absent, which is exactly what 1.3.1 forbids.

rationale: A table built out of <div class="grid-row">. It reads as a three-column table of loans to anyone who can see it, and to a screen reader it is an undifferentiated run of text with no column headers, no row boundaries and no count. A cell's value cannot be associated with the column it belongs to, so "14 March" is announced with no indication of whether it is the borrowed or the returned date.

rationale: Three radio buttons that each carry a correct individual <label>, inside a form with no fieldset and no legend. Every rule-level check passes: no input is unlabelled. What is missing is the relationship — nothing says these three options belong to one question, so a screen reader announces "Email, radio button, 1 of 3" with no statement of what is being chosen. The visible <h2> "Notify me by" supplies that to a sighted reader only.

rationale: A real <table> whose five header cells are <td>, styled to look like headers (uppercase, bold, tinted background) but carrying no <th> and no scope. rationale: The rota for the week beginning 3 August is marked up correctly — a <table> with four <th scope="col"> header cells — and then carries role="presentation", which throws all of it away. The role propagates to the rows and cells, so a screen reader announces a run of names with no shifts, no branches and no table at all. This is the case where the author did the work and cancelled it in one attribute, and it is deliberately not skipped: role="presentation" is a claim that the content carries no structure, and whether that claim is true is the whole question 1.3.1 asks.
anchor: F92: Failure of Success Criterion 1.3.1 due to the use of role presentation on content which conveys semantic information

rationale: The same rota for the week beginning 3 August, without the role. The header cells it already carried are exposed, and each name is announced with its shift and its branch.

rationale: The spring workshops are a list built out of <div> elements, each line beginning with a bullet character. The bullet is text, not list markup, so a screen reader announces five separate runs of text with no count, no start and no end. "List, five items" is what is missing, and it is what a listener uses to decide whether to skip the section or read it — a decision a sighted reader makes in a glance from the shape of the page.
